data.narrative:
Cache Energy, a Seed-stage climate and energy company founded by Arpit Dwivedi, has raised $8.5M to date and currently lacks an independent valuation. The relevant comp universe includes 1 public company (LNZA) and 8 private peers in Climate & Energy, including later-stage ventures such as Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen.

Given the absence of sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the Climate & Energy sector—only 9 peers exist globally, with insufficient narrow-filter matches—the Peer-Median method is not applicable. Instead, valuation relies on Stage-Progression methodology, which applies a typical Seed-to-next-stage multiplier of 2.5x to the $8.5M total raised proxy, yielding an implied valuation of $21M.

The triangulated valuation range is $18M to $24M, with a median of $21M, derived from a single applicable method. The primary uncertainty stems from reliance on a stage-progression heuristic rather than transaction comps; the thinness of same-stage precedent in this sector introduces model risk. Secondary uncertainties include the maturity of Cache Energy's technology, capital efficiency trajectory, and competitive positioning relative to the identified private peer set. A fuller valuation would benefit from additional comparable transactions or revenue/unit-economics data as the company progresses.
